claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C.
The proposed material contains 30% AlFeNiCoCr high-entropy-alloy binder in ZrB2.
The Al, Fe, Ni, Co, and Cr components of the binder are equimolar.
Spark plasma sintering at approximately 1500 °C will consolidate the ZrB2–AlFeNiCoCr material at a lower temperature than conventional single-phase ZrB2.
The 1500 °C cermet will be denser than conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2.
The 1500 °C cermet will be mechanically stronger and contain fewer pores than conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2.
Reduced porosity will decrease failures during prolonged exposure to liquid aluminum.
At 1500 °C, the AlFeNiCoCr binder will be liquid and sufficiently fluid to fill pores between ZrB2 grains.
The liquid binder will distribute uniformly through the ZrB2 microstructure.
Binder-assisted pore filling will improve interfacial bonding and densification.
Conventionally prepared pure ZrB2 may have larger grain boundaries because it lacks fluid-assisted pore filling.
The high-entropy-alloy binder melts at a lower temperature than pure ZrB2.
Densification and strong inter-grain bonding will impede molten-aluminum penetration and mechanical degradation.
The cermet sintered at 1500 °C will achieve a relative density near or above 97%.
The cermet sintered at 1500 °C will have higher hardness than conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2.
The cermet sintered at 1500 °C will have fracture toughness above 4.5 MPa·m^(1/2), which is asserted to be typical of pure ZrB2.
The cermet sintered at 1500 °C will have a lower molten-aluminum corrosion rate than conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2.
The cermet sintered at 1500 °C will have lower wear volume than conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2.
ZrB2–AlFeNiCoCr cermets sintered at 1300, 1400, or 1600 °C have suboptimal performance relative to the proposed 1500 °C condition.
Sintering at 1600 °C may cause binder overflow and increased porosity.
